description: A burlap sack of oats, gnawed open at one corner. Sorrel has been carrying its own feed for years.
lore: The oats are worth nothing and wet sacking less. What sells is the corner, where a farm's mark is stitched into the weave — three lines and a hook, so the mill gives you back your own sacks and not somebody else's. A collector cut that corner out and carried it round the fires, asking. [[characters/7a779de1|Wendell]] could not place it, and was short with people for a week afterwards. Four fires on, a man set his cup down and said that is my father's mark, we had it on the sacks and the gate and the churn — and then sat holding it, and could not produce his father's name, and the fire waited the way fires do. He bought the corner. He paid gold for a corner of sacking. Everyone there thought it was cheap.
gm_notes: The mark outlasts the name. Wendell's trade is remembering a road, so being stumped by a sack corner costs him something. The buyer stays unnamed on purpose.
